title_en: Ibrahim's guests and the glad tidings
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT record: it stays inside the event's own inventory refs, is shorter than the prophet story that also tells the event, and refers to that story only in general words. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims; passages from several surahs are grouped by theme and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The guests and the glad tidings

claims.statement_en: One passage tells the one addressed to inform people about the guests of Ibrahim, and another asks whether the account of Ibrahim's honoured guests has reached the listener.
Messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings; they said peace, and he answered peace.
He soon brought a roasted calf, which another passage calls a fat calf; he turned quietly to his family for it, and set it near them, asking whether they would not eat.
When he saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange and felt fear of them.
In another passage he told them that he was afraid of them.
They told him not to fear: they had been sent to the people of Lut, and they gave him glad tidings of a knowing boy.
His wife was standing there; she laughed, and they gave her glad tidings of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, of Yaqub.
She said: woe to me, shall I give birth when I am an old woman and this husband of mine is old? This is a strange thing.
In another passage she came forward with a cry, struck her face and said that she was an old woman, barren.
They said: do you wonder at God's command? God's mercy and blessings are upon you, people of the house; He is praiseworthy and glorious.
In another passage they said that it was so because her Lord had said so, and that He is the wise, the knowing.
Ibrahim asked whether they had given him glad tidings although old age had touched him, and on what basis they gave glad tidings.
They said that they had given him glad tidings in truth and that he should not be among the despairing; he said that only those who are astray despair of the mercy of their Lord.

chapters.summary_md: Messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings, and he served them a calf [c2][c3]. They told him not to fear and gave glad tidings of a boy to him and to his wife, of Ishaq and then of Yaqub [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings; they said peace, and he answered peace [c2]. He soon brought a roasted calf, and set it near them [c3]. When he saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange and felt fear of them [c4], and he told them that he was afraid [c5].

They told him not to fear: they had been sent to the people of Lut, and they gave him glad tidings of a knowing boy [c6]. His wife was standing there; she laughed, and they gave her glad tidings of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, of Yaqub [c7]. She said she was an old woman and her husband old, and called it a strange thing [c8]; in another passage she came forward with a cry, struck her face and said she was barren [c9].

The messengers asked whether she wondered at God's command, and wished mercy and blessings on the people of the house [c10]. Ibrahim asked whether they had given him glad tidings although old age had touched him [c12]. They said they had given them in truth and that he should not despair [c13], and he answered that only the astray despair of the mercy of their Lord [c13].
chapters.deep_md: The visit is told in more than one passage, each with its own details: the roasted calf and the peace greeting [c2][c3], the fear and the words that answered it [c4][c5][c6], the glad tidings to the wife and to Ibrahim [c7][c12]. Her reaction is given in different forms [c8][c9], and so is the answer of the guests [c10][c11]. The passages also open with a call to attention [c1].
chapters.kids_md: Messengers came to Ibrahim with good news [c2]. He brought them a calf, but they did not eat it, and he felt afraid [c3][c4]. They told him not to be afraid and gave him good news of a boy [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins hospitality with a surprise: the guest's food is set out before the news is given [c3][c6]. Another is that Ibrahim answers the news by saying that only the astray despair of their Lord's mercy [c13].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the messengers were, how many they were, or what form they had; the verses call them messengers and guests only.
- Not established: where Ibrahim lived at the time, or the age of Ibrahim and his wife; the verses speak of old age but give no numbers.
- The Arabic word for her laughing (11:71) is understood in more than one way; a scholar should decide the rendering.
- The identity of the knowing boy of 15:53 and 51:28, and its relation to the glad tidings of Ishaq in 11:71, is read in more than one way; this draft does not decide.
- The wife is not named in these verses.
- The passages 11:69-73, 15:51-56 and 51:24-30 are read as one visit on matching wording (an inference).

claims.statement_en: Ibrahim asked the messengers what their business was.
They said that they had been sent to a people of criminals, to send down on them stones of clay marked with their Lord for those who exceed all bounds.
The family of Lut would be saved, all of them, except his wife, whom God had decreed to be among those who stay behind.
When the fear had left Ibrahim and the glad tidings had come to him, he began to plead with God about the people of Lut.
God describes Ibrahim as forbearing, awwah and turning back to Him, awwah being a word understood in more than one way.
Ibrahim was told to turn away from this, for the command of his Lord had come and a punishment that could not be turned back was coming to them.
God says that He brought out the believers who were in it, and found in it only one house of those who submitted.
God says that He left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.

chapters.summary_md: Ibrahim asked the messengers what their business was, and they said they were sent to a people of criminals, but the family of Lut would be saved [c1][c2][c3]. Ibrahim pleaded with God about the people of Lut and was told to turn away from this [c4][c6].
chapters.body_md:
Ibrahim asked the messengers what their business was [c1]. They said that they had been sent to a people of criminals, to send down on them stones of clay marked with their Lord [c2]. The family of Lut would be saved, all of them, except his wife, whom God had decreed to be among those who stay behind [c3].

When the fear had left Ibrahim and the glad tidings had come to him, he began to plead with God about the people of Lut [c4]. God describes Ibrahim as forbearing, awwah and turning back to Him [c5]. He was told to turn away from this, for the command of his Lord had come and a punishment that could not be turned back was coming to them [c6].

God says He brought out the believers who were in it and found only one house of those who submitted [c7], and that He left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The later part of the visit turns from the glad tidings to the sending [c1][c2]. The exception for the family of Lut and the one who stays behind [c3] is told in one passage, Ibrahim's pleading in another [c4][c5][c6], and the outcome in yet another [c7][c8]. The passages differ in what they include, and the pleading is told only in 11:74-76 [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Ibrahim asked the messengers why they had come [c1]. They said they were sent to a people who did wrong, but that the family of Lut would be saved [c2][c3]. Ibrahim pleaded for them, and was told to turn away from this [c4][c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that God's description of Ibrahim as forbearing and turning back to Him sits beside his pleading [c4][c5]. Another is that the passage records a limit: a command that had come could not be turned back [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name of the place, how long it took, or how the believers were brought out.
- Not established: how many were in the one house of those who submitted.
- The word awwah (11:75) is rendered in different ways, for example tender-hearted or one who often calls on God; a scholar should decide.
- The wife of Lut is not named in these verses.
- The pronoun in 51:35-37, rendered 'it', refers to a place the verses do not name here.
- The inventory range stops at these ayat; the destruction itself is told elsewhere and is not part of this record.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the visit of the messengers to Ibrahim. None is used in this draft.
The visit is also told inside the longer story of Ibrahim (content/stories/ibrahim.draft.json); this record is a shorter account that refers to it only in general words.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the messengers, of Ibrahim's wife and of the place. None is used in the story texts.
The passages are read as one visit on matching wording (an inference); the details differ between them.
The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of the chapters is a reading order only.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
